Australian federal police arrested and charged two men after allegedly finding 2.7 tonnes of cocaine in ‘bunkers’ under shipping containers Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Police have made what they say is Australia’s biggest ever cocaine seizure, uncovering 2.7 tonnes of the drug buried in secret bunkers at a property on Sydney’s western fringes. The seizure was made by the Australian federal police on Friday at a semi-rural property in Londonderry. Two men aged 21 and 25 have been arrested and charged with possessing a commercial quantity of an unlawfully imported border-controlled drug. Police allege they found the drugs in plastic tubs buried in underground bunkers concealed beneath three shipping containers on the property.

They said the cocaine had an estimated street value of about $816m, equating to about 3 million “street-level deals”. Police allege the cocaine was imported into Australia near Midge Point in north Queensland and brought to Sydney “at the behest of a Sydney organised crime group”. The seizure was part of Operation Minjiang, a joint investigation by the AFP alongside Queensland police, the Australian Border Force and other agencies. It began after 40kg of cocaine was allegedly found in the water off a boat ramp at Midge Point on the Whitsunday Coast. An alleged “mother vessel” suspected to be part of a drug importation enterprise, MV Wealth, has been detained in the Solomon Islands.

[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Australian federal police arrested and charged two men after allegedly finding 2.7 tonnes of cocaine in ‘bunkers’ under shipping containers

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Police have made what they say is Australia’s biggest ever cocaine seizure, uncovering 2.7 tonnes of the drug buried in secret bunkers at a property on Sydney’s western fringes.

The seizure was made by the Australian federal police on Friday at a semi-rural property in Londonderry.

Two men aged 21 and 25 have been arrested and charged with possessing a commercial quantity of an unlawfully imported border-controlled drug.

Police allege they found the drugs in plastic tubs buried in underground bunkers concealed beneath three shipping containers on the property.

They said the cocaine had an estimated street value of about $816m, equating to about 3 million “street-level deals”.

Police allege the cocaine was imported into Australia near Midge Point in north Queensland and brought to Sydney “at the behest of a Sydney organised crime group”.

The seizure was part of Operation Minjiang, a joint investigation by the AFP alongside Queensland police, the Australian Border Force and other agencies. It began after 40kg of cocaine was allegedly found in the water off a boat ramp at Midge Point on the Whitsunday Coast.

An alleged “mother vessel” suspected to be part of a drug importation enterprise, MV Wealth, has been detained in the Solomon Islands.

The two men arrested on Friday appeared before a NSW local court on Saturday and were remanded in custody. They are next expected to appear before Penrith local court on 13 August.

She suffered critical injuries when she became trapped beneath the Hyundai i30 hatchback about 11.30pm on Saturday, May 16.

Bystanders worked to lift the car off the young woman, and Kaur was taken to Royal Perth Hospital fighting for life, but died shortly after.

The alleged driver of the car involved, a 19-year-old Forrestfield man, was questioned by police at the time, and was charged over the death on Saturday, WA Police said on Monday.

He was charged with careless driving causing death, grievous bodily harm or bodily harm, and will face Armadale Magistrates Court on July 3.

Two cars have been in a serious crash in South Australia.

They crashed on Glenroy St in Athol Park about 5.45am on Monday.

One of the cars appears to have flipped on its side.

Glenroy St has been closed off and traffic is being diverted via Lavinia St and Milicent St.

It is unclear if the drivers were injured in the crash.

The highway was closed to traffic but has since reopened.

Investigations in the crash are ongoing.

A truck has burst into flames on a highway east of Perth.

One of the trailer brakes caught fire before the blaze spread to engulf the whole vehicle.

The driver pulled over and got out of the truck uninjured.

Truck drivers banked up on the blocked off highway as firefighters extinguished the fire.

payload.title: Australian poliisi takavarikoi 2,7 tonnia kokaiinia Sydneyn laidalla
payload.summary: Australian liittovaltion poliisi kertoo tehneensä maan historian suurimman kokaiinitakavarikon löydettyään 2,7 tonnia huumetta maahan kätketyistä bunkkereista Sydneyn länsireunalla.
payload.content:
Australian liittovaltion poliisi kertoo takavarikoineensa 2,7 tonnia kokaiinia puoliksi maaseutumaiselta kiinteistöltä Londonderrystä Sydneyn länsilaidalta. Poliisin mukaan kyseessä on Australian historian suurin kokaiinitakavarikko, ja löydön jälkeen kaksi miestä on pidätetty ja asetettu syytteeseen epäillystä laittomasti maahan tuodun rajavalvotun huumausaineen kaupallisen määrän hallussapidosta.

## Huumeet löytyivät konttien alta

Poliisin mukaan kokaiini oli piilotettu muoviastioihin maanalaisiin bunkkereihin, jotka oli kätketty kolmen rahtikontin alle. Takavarikko tehtiin perjantaina kiinteistöllä Sydneyn läntisillä reuna-alueilla. Syytetyt miehet ovat poliisin mukaan 21- ja 25-vuotiaita.

Viranomaiset arvioivat takavarikoidun kokaiinin katuarvoksi noin 816 miljoonaa Australian dollaria. Poliisin mukaan määrä vastaisi noin kolmea miljoonaa katukaupan annosta, mikä kuvaa takavarikon poikkeuksellista kokoa Australian huumetutkinnassa.

## Reittiä jäljitetään Queenslandista Sydneyyn

Poliisi epäilee, että kokaiini tuotiin Australiaan lähellä Midge Pointia Pohjois-Queenslandissa ja kuljetettiin sieltä Sydneyyn Sydneyssä toimivan järjestäytyneen rikollisryhmän toimeksiannosta. Poliisin julkistamien tietojen mukaan Londonderryn löytö liittyy laajempaan maahantuontiepäilyyn.

Takavarikko on osa Operation Minjiang -nimistä yhteistutkintaa. Siihen osallistuvat Australian liittovaltion poliisin lisäksi Queenslandin poliisi, Australian rajaviranomaiset ja muita viranomaisia.

## Tutkinta alkoi rannikon löydöstä

Tutkinta käynnistyi sen jälkeen, kun Midge Pointin veneluiskan edustalta Whitsunday Coastilla väitetään löytyneen 40 kiloa kokaiinia vedestä. Viranomaiset ovat myös ottaneet Salomonsaarilla haltuun MV Wealth -nimisen aluksen, jota epäillään osaksi huumeiden maahantuontiin liittyvää järjestelyä.

Poliisin julkistamien tietojen perusteella syytteet koskevat tässä vaiheessa kahden miehen väitettyä osuutta kaupallisen huumemäärän hallussapitoon. Kokonaisuuden tutkinta jatkuu usean viranomaisen yhteistyönä.
